description: The mix, read by the page alone: how loud each family of sounds is heard against the others, and how the bed is made gentle. Each bus's level is in dB, under the player's slider; the sea bus is shelved down above shelf.frequency by shelf.gain dB. The master runs into a safety limiter (threshold dB, knee dB, ratio, attack and release s) that the mix is staged to keep away from. fades: s to fade in at the start, out on mute or hide, in on unmute or show, a slider's glide and the voices' glide (a time constant). bed: the sea's voices' levels as the recipes give them are played as most times (level / most) to the power curve, so a breeze and a gale are nearer than the recipes have them; trims are each voice's dB in the mix. calm: a quiet lapping at the hull while the boat drifts, its band (Hz, q) and level falling away over speed m/s, swelling every period s, each lap from rest to most. tone: the bow wave's hiss's band, Hz; the rigging sings only in gusts, from gust.from to gust.full of the wind's gust factor, its band's q; the gun's crack is low-passed at gunCrack Hz; birds' and colonies' harmonic calls are low-passed at birds.lowpass times their pitch and swell in over birds.attack s. noise: the seconds of each of the white, pink and brown noises the voices read, each at its own offset. layers: the bed's families, each played by its recordings where they have loaded (recorded/*.json) and by its synthesis the share they leave, a recording taking over over crossfade s; a family of several layers crossfades them at equal power between their centres at, on its scale: the apparent wind, m/s (the wind, whose recordings' low-pass opens from lowpass[0] to lowpass[1] Hz and gain rises by gust.gain dB from gust.from to gust.full of the gust factor); the speed as a share of the hull speed (the hull); the sea's height, m, with whitecaps times its whitecaps (the sea); the rain, mm an hour. match is the dB a recording at -23 LUFS plays at over its family's level to be as loud as the synthesis, as the tests measure it. shots: the same for a shot's recordings, at a true peak of -1.5 dBTP. slaps: the bow meeting a wave, from a pitch rate (rad/s) falling past pitchRate[0] and full at pitchRate[1], heave of it from the hull dropping (heaveRate, m/s), at most every least s, at level; synthesised as a burst through a band falling from band[1] to band[0] Hz at q dying over decay s, and a thump Hz at thumpLevel, varied pitch semitones and spread dB. sail: the boom past side rad of the centreline crossing; a tack where the apparent wind is within tack degrees of the bow, the sheet running (level, rising with the apparent wind over wind m/s, length s, a band Hz at q fluttering at rate Hz); else a gybe, the boom's thump (level by its rate, rad/s; thump Hz, decay s, a knock's band Hz at q). halyards: in port, from wind[0] to wind[1] m/s of apparent wind, at level, a swing every every[0] to every[1] s, its answer pair s later; each tap a band of tone Hz at q dying over decay s. surf: a shore's, as the water shoals from depth[0] to depth[1] m and the sea rises from height[0] to height[1] m, at level, swelling every period s, a band of centre Hz at q.
